Definition: from G4912; restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety:--anguish, distress.
BiblicalUsage: Upon the earth there will be distress of nations, with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring, and Paul writes to the Corinthians out of much affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears. Distress can be the world's end or a pastor's heart, and in both cases it is a squeezing that leaves no way out but God.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that distress drives us to God when nothing else will, and I hold that Paul's tears over Corinth show me what a shepherd's anguish is for.
